newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sets up deposit insurance scheme.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sets up deposit insurance scheme.

text.p: Bank of Thailand deputy governor Siri Garnjarerndee said on Friday the central bank has set up a federal deposit insurance scheme aimed mainly at protecting deposits of banks and finance companies still open.
Siri told a news conference the guaranteees should last for about two years and should help bring down deposit rates which he said are "too high."
Siri said the deposit scheme will also apply to any of the 58 suspended finance companies if they manage to rehabilitate themselves under guidelines and in the timeframe set by the central bank.
He said current deposit rates, between 10-11.5 percent for major banks, were too high. He said the deposit insurance scheme was in line guidelines from the International Monetary Fund.

On Tuesday the government announced the suspension of 42 finance firms, on top of 16 already suspended in June. Authorities said the suspensions were made in an effort to reform the finance sector and separate good firms from bad.

The governent said on Tuesday the 42 cash-strapped finance companies had borrowed about 430 billion baht ($13.9 billion) from the central bank to help solve their liquidity problems. The finance companies were given 60 days to set up a rehabilitation plan.
Jittery markets reacted negatively to the surprise announcement as many investors were unsure about the fate of the country's remaining 33 finance companies.
Siri's news conference and the announcement of the deposit insurance scheme was part of an effort by the central bank and other financial authorities to bring confidence back to the market.
